findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly specify how `_usage` surfaces from `pass1_chunk` / `pass1_container` / `pass1_isf` up to `run_pass1` (e.g. change each to return `(findings, usage_dict)`, or introduce a thread-local/ContextVar side-channel), since those functions discard `result["_usage"]` today and `run_pass1` never sees a raw runner result.
evidence: passes.py:331: `result = runner.run(req)` — usage consumed inside pass1_chunk, not returned
passes.py:332-360: `out` is a filtered findings list; `result["_usage"]` is not included
pass1.py:458: `out = _pass1_with_ladder(...)` — returns list[dict], no usage carrier
pass1.py:486-492: futures yield findings lists only
Plan says: 'Accumulate `_usage` across every runner.run call inside run_pass1'
findings.finding: `runner.run` is called inside `passes.pass1_chunk`, `passes.pass1_container`, and `passes.pass1_isf` — those functions return `list[dict]` (findings only) and discard `result["_usage"]` before returning. `run_pass1` never sees a raw runner result; it only ever receives findings lists from `_pass1_with_ladder` / `_timed_pairing` / direct `pass1_isf` calls. The plan's stated mechanism — 'accumulate `_usage` across every runner.run call inside run_pass1' — has no access point in `run_pass1` as it stands; the accumulation can only happen if `pass1_chunk`, `pass1_container`, and `pass1_isf` are changed to also return (or side-channel) their `_usage` alongside findings. The plan names both files in scope but does not articulate this required interface change.
scenarios: Implementer writes usage accumulation in run_pass1 but finds no _usage key anywhere in the data it receives — totals stay zero, the same gap the plan is trying to fix.
Implementer modifies pass1_chunk to return (findings, usage) — breaking every existing call site not listed in the plan's scope.
findings.suggested_fix: The simplest codebase-aligned fix: change `pass1_chunk` to return `(list[dict], dict)` (findings + usage), propagate the same change to `pass1_container` and `pass1_isf`, and update `pass1_with_ladder` to thread usage through its ladder rung returns. All three callers in `run_pass1` then receive usage alongside findings. Alternatively, use a `contextvars.ContextVar` accumulator that `runner.run` writes to (it already copies context per worker thread via `_submit_ctx`), letting `run_pass1` read the total after joining futures without touching pass1_chunk's signature.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify which intermediate layer(s) must be modified to propagate `_usage` back to `run_pass1` (e.g. have `passes.pass1_chunk` return a `(findings, usage)` tuple, or have `_chunk` capture `_usage` via a nonlocal accumulator).
evidence: pass1.py:444-459: `_chunk` calls `_pass1_with_ladder(runner, cfg, plan, chunk, agentic, ladder_events, extra)` and returns its result directly — findings only, no _usage.
passes.py:331: `pass1_chunk` calls `runner.run(req)` and returns findings extracted from `result.get('findings')` — the `result['_usage']` is discarded.
pass1.py:487-491: The pool futures collect `fu.result()` from `_chunk`, which returns findings — no _usage propagation path exists today.
Similarly, `pass1_container` (passes.py:430) calls `runner.run` and discards `result['_usage']` before returning findings.
findings.finding: The plan says to 'accumulate `_usage` across every runner.run call inside run_pass1,' but `run_pass1` does NOT call `runner.run` directly — it goes through `_chunk` → `_pass1_with_ladder` (sizing.pass1_with_ladder) → `passes.pass1_chunk` → `runner.run`. The intermediate functions (`_pass1_with_ladder`, `passes.pass1_chunk`) return only findings lists, not the raw result dict that carries `_usage`. The plan never specifies which layer must be modified to surface `_usage` back to `run_pass1`, leaving the accumulation placement ambiguous.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Accumulate `_usage` across every runner.run call inside run_pass1 (single-turn chunks, AGENT criteria, container pairings, prerequisite calls)'
scenarios: An implementer modifying only `run_pass1` cannot see `_usage` because every intermediate function strips it before returning.
The implementer must decide whether to modify passes.pass1_chunk, pass1.py:_chunk, sizing.pass1_with_ladder, or all three — a non-trivial API surface change not scoped in the plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify whether per-criterion usage accumulation is sequential or concurrent; if concurrent, specify a thread-safe accumulation mechanism (e.g., per-call local dicts merged after all calls complete, or a lock-protected shared dict).
evidence: ABSENCE: No mention of locks, thread-safe collections, or sequential-only constraint on the accumulation step.
The plan references 'production_batch_runner.py', a batch runner that by name implies concurrent execution of multiple criteria.
The accumulation covers multiple distinct call categories, suggesting iteration over multiple criteria — likely in parallel given the 'batch' framing.
findings.finding: The plan accumulates _usage across 'every runner.run call inside run_pass1 (single-turn chunks, AGENT criteria, container pairings, prerequisite calls)' into a shared per-criterion map, but does not specify whether these calls are sequential or concurrent. If criteria are processed in parallel (consistent with the existing batch-runner architecture), the shared accumulation dict is mutated from multiple threads/coroutines without any synchronization primitive, creating a TOCTOU/race condition.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Accumulate _usage across every runner.run call inside run_pass1 (single-turn chunks, AGENT criteria, container pairings, prerequisite calls)'
scenarios: Two criteria processed concurrently both read-then-increment the same counter in the usage dict; one update is lost (classic lost-update race).
Partial accumulation is read by the consumer before all concurrent criteria have finished writing, producing undercount token totals in the sidecar.
findings.suggested_fix: Accumulate _usage locally per runner.run call into a list of dicts, then merge/sum them into the aggregate and per-criterion map after all calls complete (a collect-then-reduce pattern that is inherently race-free).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the concurrency strategy for usage accumulation (e.g. collect per-future usage from each `fu.result()` call sequentially after futures complete, or use a lock around a shared accumulator) so concurrent chunk futures cannot race on the totals.
evidence: pass1.py:486-492: `ThreadPoolExecutor` with up to 6 workers; futures resolved by iterating `st_futs + ag_futs`
Plan: 'Accumulate `_usage` across every runner.run call inside run_pass1' — no mention of synchronisation
Container fan-out also concurrent (_CONTAINER_MAX_WORKERS=6)
findings.finding: The plan is silent on thread-safety of usage accumulation. `run_pass1` fans out single-turn chunks and agent criteria concurrently in a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (pass1.py:486-492). Any shared mutable accumulator (e.g. a plain `dict` summed across futures) written from multiple worker threads without synchronisation is a data race that produces silently incorrect totals.
scenarios: Two chunk futures both read and update the shared totals dict concurrently, producing a lost update and an under-counted token total.
Race is intermittent and test doubles with stub usage (as specified in Testing) may not expose it since FakeRunner calls are synchronous in unit tests.
findings.suggested_fix: The simplest safe approach: each future returns `(findings, usage)` alongside results; the sequential `for fu in st_futs + ag_futs: findings.extend(fu.result())` loop is already the join point — accumulate into a local sum there (single thread, no lock needed).
